title: Your checkout is 4 fields too long.
styleLine: ONE CONSISTENT LINE ACROSS ALL IMAGES (critical). Cinematic editorial photography, shot as if by the SAME photographer on the SAME 35mm lens, natural white-balance (5200-5500K), rich but neutral grade — deep near-black shadows, clean daylight highlights (NO warm cream cast, NO heavy Instagram filter, NOT washed-out, NOT HDR). A modern small software-studio workspace: walnut desks, natural window light, plants, notebooks and coffee cups; laptops and phones sit clean on the surface, straight-on, front-facing (see straight-on device rule) when a screen is in frame. Slight teal-to-neutral color palette overall — reads as a systems-engineering studio's photography, not agency stock. NO branded gear, NO logos visible on any screen, NO stock 'business meeting' props. 4:5 aspect (1080x1350), designed for Instagram feed carousels (full frame visible) and TikTok photo carousels. SAFE ZONES: (a) Instagram profile grid crops to CENTER 1:1 — top ~135px and bottom ~135px cropped in grid view — keep the hero subject center-frame. (b) TikTok photo mode overlays a caption/UI region across the bottom ~340px on the visible feed — keep critical visual detail above that band. (c) The lower ~40% of the frame (roughly y=810 to y=1350) is reserved for on-slide type — compose the subject in the upper ~55-60% but fill the ENTIRE frame with natural scene content — NO dark band, NO black rectangle, NO artificial dark area. A CSS gradient handles text legibility. No text, no logos, no clearly identifiable faces (backs of heads, hands, over-the-shoulder crops are fine). Anti-band: no dark gradient, no vignette, no overlay, only natural light falloff; one single continuous photograph natively 4:5, do NOT letterbox, pad, extend or outpaint.
note: Path B. Slides 2 and 5 use device composites (phone-book + laptop-hero). Others are pure editorial photos.

slides.headline: Your ==checkout== is 4 fields too long.
slides.sub: Every field is a customer you almost had.

slides.imagePrompt: A phone lying face-up on a walnut desk, PERFECTLY STRAIGHT AND FRONT-ON, ZERO rotation, ZERO tilt, screen filling most of the frame from a shallow overhead angle. The screen is plain white (a Kymbo booking-app UI will be composited on top later). A hand rests near the phone but not touching the screen; a coffee cup and pen in soft focus. Natural cool daylight. Compose the subject in the UPPER ~55-60% of the frame. CRITICAL: fill the ENTIRE frame with natural scene content — NO dark band, NO black rectangle, NO artificial dark area at the bottom. A CSS overlay handles text readability. [Apply the STYLE LINE.]
slides.title: Count the ==required== fields.
slides.body: Address, city, state, zip, country, phone, email, first, last. Nine minimum. Every one that doesn't need to be there deletes 1-3% of conversion — run the math on your own store, not ours.

slides.imagePrompt: Close overhead of a paper notebook on a walnut desk, a hand holding a rollerball pen mid-stroke; the notebook page has abstract, non-readable pencil marks (short horizontal lines suggesting a list, no readable words). A coffee cup, a plant, natural cool daylight. Compose the subject in the UPPER ~55-60% of the frame. CRITICAL: fill the ENTIRE frame with natural scene content — NO dark band, NO black rectangle, NO artificial dark area at the bottom. A CSS overlay handles text readability. [Apply the STYLE LINE.]
slides.title: The ==four== we cut first.
slides.body: Address line 2 (nobody uses it). Phone (unless you're shipping and dispatch actually calls). Company name (unless you're B2B). Confirm-email (2005-era paranoia). Cut them and re-measure.

slides.imagePrompt: A hand holding a phone at chest level in a workspace; the phone screen is plain white (no UI). Thumb hovers over the screen mid-decision. Natural cool daylight, walnut desk in soft focus behind. Compose the subject in the UPPER ~55-60% of the frame. CRITICAL: fill the ENTIRE frame with natural scene content — NO dark band, NO black rectangle, NO artificial dark area at the bottom. A CSS overlay handles text readability. [Apply the STYLE LINE.]
slides.title: The fields aren't the point. The ==friction== is.
slides.body: Every keystroke on mobile is a moment the thumb hovers over the back button. Our job on Shopify and Woo builds isn't to add fields you might want — it's to hold the line against them.

slides.imagePrompt: A laptop open on a walnut desk, PERFECTLY STRAIGHT AND FRONT-ON, ZERO rotation, ZERO tilt, viewed straight-on from a slightly elevated angle so the full screen is visible. The screen is plain white (a Kymbo analytics dashboard UI will be composited on top later). A coffee cup and notebook beside it. Natural cool daylight. Compose the subject in the UPPER ~55-60% of the frame. CRITICAL: fill the ENTIRE frame with natural scene content — NO dark band, NO black rectangle, NO artificial dark area at the bottom. A CSS overlay handles text readability. [Apply the STYLE LINE.]
slides.title: Track abandonment by ==field==, not by page.
slides.body: Page-level analytics tells you "they left the checkout." Field-level tells you which field they left on. If you can't see which field killed the sale, you can't fix it.

slides.headline: We ship checkouts by what you ==remove==.
slides.sub: Nine fields is a starting number. Not a ceiling.
